absence_description: Standard accrued paid time off for rest and recreation.
Time off for the birth, adoption, or fostering of a child (can be paid or unpaid depending on jurisdiction).
Flexible paid days off that employees can use at their discretion.
An extended career break (often paid or partially paid) for research, travel, or skill acquisition.
Country-specific official days off (e.g., Christmas, Labor Day).
Extended time off for significant health treatments or surgeries.
Paid or unpaid time off following the death of a family member.
Mandatory absence when summoned to serve on a legal jury.
An unauthorised, unexcused absence from work (a disciplinary infraction).
Time off to prepare for or sit professional examinations.
Authorised absence where the employee does not receive a salary but retains their job.
Time off for active duty, deployment, or mandatory military reserve training.
Short, legally mandated absence to cast a ballot on election days.
Multi-month or multi-year absence for chronic or severe health conditions.
